# Get-HyperVInventory

<!-- Generated by tools/Build-Catalog.ps1. Edit the script header, not this file. -->

Inventories virtual machines on one or more Hyper-V hosts and writes an HTML report (optional CSV).

| | |
|---|---|
| Location | `scripts/windows/server/Get-HyperVInventory.ps1` |
| Platform | Windows (Hyper-V PowerShell module on the machine running the script) |
| Permissions | Hyper-V Administrators (or local admin) on each host; WinRM/WMI access for remote hosts |
| Safety | Read-only |

## When to use

Capacity planning, documenting a customer's virtual estate, or finding VMs with forgotten snapshots before maintenance.

## Description

Connects to each host with the Hyper-V PowerShell module and lists every VM with state, vCPU count,
startup memory, uptime, generation, status and configuration version. Optional switches also collect
snapshots, network adapters and virtual hard disks per VM (held in memory; the HTML and CSV show the
snapshot count). Output is an HTML report with a summary header, plus an optional CSV.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-ComputerName` | String[] | No | One or more Hyper-V hosts. Default: the local machine. Old name: HyperVHosts. |
| `-OutputPath` | String | No | Folder for the report. Falls back to $env:TOOLBOX_REPORT_DIR, then prompts. |
| `-CustomerName` | String | No | Optional. Adds a &lt;OutputPath&gt;\&lt;CustomerName&gt; subfolder. |
| `-ExportCsv` | SwitchParameter | No | Also write a CSV of the VM list next to the HTML report. |
| `-IncludeSnapshots` | SwitchParameter | No | Collect checkpoint (snapshot) details and show a snapshot badge next to VMs that have them. |
| `-IncludeNetworks` | SwitchParameter | No | Collect virtual network adapter details for each VM. |
| `-IncludeStorage` | SwitchParameter | No | Collect virtual hard disk details for each VM. |

## Examples

```powershell
.\Get-HyperVInventory.ps1 -OutputPath D:\Reports
```

```powershell
.\Get-HyperVInventory.ps1 -ComputerName HV01,HV02 -IncludeSnapshots -ExportCsv -OutputPath D:\Reports -CustomerName Contoso
```
